turns.text: Hey, what's up—this is Zach here at the Gen Z on Media House, the GN Podcast in Bangkok, Thailand. Super excited to be talking about staking. I'll let our next guest introduce herself. If you want to say your name, the company you're with, and your position at the company.
Uh, yeah, for sure. Nice to meet you. My name is Anna, I'm head of R&D at EverStake, and we are the biggest one staking provider.
Wow, okay, that's amazing. You say "the biggest" staking provider?

Uh, yeah, the biggest one staking provider for the number of our users. So we have 735,000 unique users, I mean stakers, so yeah, and it feels pretty, pretty good to deliver our service to the community.

Very cool. So I think R&D is very interesting, and I find it fascinating that you are on the podcast, because we usually don't get to speak to people who are interested in R&D on camera. So kind of, what is that like, being in, you know, R&D in the staking?

So it's pretty interesting, because we are in R&D, taking care of all the new projects that appear on the market. So we conduct an R&D research, doing our modeling—project lifecycle modeling, economic modeling—and talk to the project team and decide if this project is promising enough. So EverStake can join on an operational level as a validator, I mean, and support the project and deliver the service for staking to the community. So it's like deep research work, and we are feel excited on this part because it's allowed to get some insight, to get some, like, correlations, and still have a deep dive in project economics and model it. So pretty cool.
No, I completely agree. And I think we were chatting before, can you talk about maybe some of the ecosystems that you guys support? Because I know there's a lot of different projects.
Yeah, definitely. So the biggest one, I believe, is Cicero, for sure.
I think people have probably heard of that, yeah.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. So it's pretty good as it appears on different levelsright now. So it's Cicero, native staking, liquid staking, re-staking. Actually, we're operating on all of these three levels at EverStake, and it's quite different target audience on each of them. So some levels are mostly institutional, some levels are mostly for retail, and some, like, newly appearance level, like re-staking, is pretty excited also for both parts. So we are deep inside on a, like, database scientific level of researching and modeling that's the most, like, hot topics here. So what will be the APR for re-staking, how the session will works there, so how the service will works there for, like, end users, and what you can expect and what you can achieve. So this is a case, for sure, like bull shark-based projects feel pretty excited. So I mean, it's like captives, it's UE projects, newly appeared Aleo, very nice L1 project as well. So yeah, we're also expecting a few more strong L1 projects this year, so it will be the first quarter they should launch their main net.
Any you want to shout out that you're excited for?
Um, yeah, why not. So we're expecting the particle network.
Oh yeah, particle, that's a big one.

Yeah, this is for the main net launch, Wallet Connect network. Actually, yesterday they announced the official date of staking launch, I believe it's end of November. What else? It's a few test nets, like Walrus test nets, just launched, Space and Time test net will be launched very soon, I believe this quarter as well. So yeah, and a few more, like Story Protocol, Beaver Chain, expected next phases of Babylon as well. So pretty wide range and different types of projects in the top rate.
What do you think that people don't understand about staking? Like, what's a common misconception that you think you hear that people should know?

Um, the most common? So it depends on the type of user we talk about. So for institutional, it's different types of concerns and miscommunications and misunderstandings. For the retail, the most part, I believe it's the difference between staking and DeFi projects and products that appear on the market. So where end users should understand that if he stakes, he helps to secure the ecosystem, and he helps to secure the blockchain itself with his funds. So he stakes to validator on a proof of stake concept and helps to secure the blockchain. And on a DeFi project, it's a different type of activity and, like, earning specific income. So it's like very, very different structure here. So it's like the most, the most common, I guess.

Which one would you say, I mean, I—this is probably odd—what is the one you say is safer? Like, why do you think? Because I think staking is much, much safer. I mean, and sort of securing the blockchain. Can you kind of explain that to people who maybe don't understand?

Uh, yeah, for sure. It's linked to the concept how proof of stake networks work itself. So it's a set of validators, each validator running their nodes, yeah, on the technical level of operations. And so users can stake their money to the validator. So it's like non-custodial, fully non-custodial way. And with the stake, validator produce the blocks on the network, so on the blockchain itself, and confirm the transactions. And the blockchain exists according to this part. And actually, it's allowed to get it move with the blocks forward, and it's allowed to prevent any malicious actions in the blockchain for, like, any validators or other malicious players.

No, I think that's really important. I think—thank you for breaking that down, because a lot of people talk about it, and you actually broke it down, like, very eloquently. So I really appreciate that. Can you maybe talk about, like, what the advantage is for staking with you guys versus maybe another platform? Like, you know, say I have, like, a million dollars to stake, why would I stake with you guys?

Um, I believe it depends mostly on the technical level of operations. So it should be, it should be a trusted party. So it not depends you will choose EverStake or any other. It should be a trusted party. And it's important to hold all the operations in-house. So for example, in EverStake, we have around 60 people in the develop staff. So we hold all our operations in-house, and our uptime is 99.9%. So it's—
Happens the other 0.1. No, just kidding, just kidding.
It depends on the consensus mechanism.
Just kidding, yeah. That's very good.

It's actually, it's important because, you know, some consensus mechanism allowed to keep, like, 100% uptime, and some consensus mechanism, it's very good. If it's, like, 99 there, it's like top achievement.
Got you.

Yeah. So yeah, technical level of operations is very important. And the quality of nodes, backup servers, strict security policy, strict technical policy of operations. So it should be like a trusted provider that could guarantee you as an end user that it will be top performed. And you should be interested in this part not only for, like, some slashes or some losing of your money, and also for, like, a top APR. Because as better the performance of staking providers, the better APR you will get as an end user.
And that's really, I mean, that's key,right? You always want to go where the APR is the highest and, of course, the most secure.
Yes.

That's super interesting. What, I guess, for you with the market kind of like pumpingright now, there's obviously a lot of new capital coming into crypto, what do you see the future of staking? Like, where do you see this market going in the next 5, even 10 years?
Oh, I believe it's hard to say for, like, 10 years.
Even years, let's say 6 months.

Yeah, yeah. Yeah, so we actually predicting and conducting our market research in depth for, like, one year ahead. And yeah, we expecting some interesting trends coming on the market. So for sure, for sure, re-staking will developed, and we'll expect the expand to other ecosystem. It will be not only Ceroom. We expect Solana ecosystem re-staking quite some high level. Also, it's like BTC, BTC re-staking and walled projects. So we expect on Symbiotic, Babylon, DLC BTC, and some other projects will be strong on this part.
Why do you think BTC staking is so low as a percentage of market cap compared to, like, Ethereum?

Uh, because it's only, only emerging trend. So it's just started, let's say, a year or a year and a half ago. And the projects on BTC staking, re-staking is pretty youngright now. And it also depends on the project quality, you know, because it's when it's a load of, like, smart contracts inside, when it's very long road inside there, it couldn't be, like, trusted or secure enough to participate in, I mean, for big players. So we should wait to it to stabilize a bit. And we should wait for some, like, big projects, stable projects. So we'll launch their main nets with BTC staking, and we expect that this direction should grow enough on the market.
Do you see particular companies moving in that direction?

For BTC staking? Uh, yeah, sure. We expect in Babylon, it's already launched on main net, it should be, like, another cap opening soon. We're looking closely for Symbiotic and also operate on Symbiotic, and it should be BTC vaults inside there with the different options with, like, good trusted market players. I mean, LRTs and all the related stuff should run in this part. Also, some, like, XR, DLC BTC, core projects. So pretty strong, and I think they will get quite huge market share.
I completely agree. I think XR, the one that you called out, is really cool. We work with them, and I think they're doing an excellent job.
Oh, yeah, we actually operate on an XR as well, so.

Oh, very cool. So mutual, mutual connections there. Yeah, those guys are great. Kind of bringing it back to where we are here, which is in Thailand. How has the event been for you so far? What's kind of the goal for the team here, if there is one? Or if not, just having fun, because it is very fun.
Yeah.
I know there's a lot of work to be done, so.
Yeah, yeah, it's a lot of work, actually. It's a lot of stuff to do. It's a lot of our partners here. So it's like 900 side events during this week.
Yeah, I read something that said if the average side event is like 10 grand, that's $9 million spent on side events this week. Isn't that crazy?
Yeah, it's amazing.
Yeah, $9 million spent in Thailand. So they obviously love having the event here. If you think about all the money that's coming in, but sorry to interrupt, but yeah, it is crazy.

Yeah, yeah, definitely. Definitely. And, you know, it's expected to be a lot of, a lot of people here and a lot of new projects here. So we have mostly our, like, partners meetings here from R&D side, I mean. And we are hosting, co-hosting two events. So please join us. It will be tomorrow, AVS Café with Sandeep. And it should be ASD, should be pretty huge with consensus. And it should be almost all AVS is on re-staking level and some debate. So should be very active. I feel pretty excited on this part. Yeah, so welcome, please join us.
What's the debate on?

Debates, it will be like four different tracks for the debate. First, the debates for ours one, it will be the most hottest topic, I believe, in re-staking. It will be regarding slashing, regarding centralization on the re-staking part, and operation of on the market with, like, multiple AVSs for operators. So I believe it's the most discussable part of re-stakingright now, because everybody feel excited and guessing how the slashing conditions will look like and how users can manage the risk on this part and how to prevent some not desirable situation on this part and what to expect, etc., etc. So yeah, we will have pretty, pretty nice players here. It will be like consensus team, it will be out there team, EverStake team as well, and we will try to figure out the best, the best solutions and keys.
That's amazing. And kind of how big? You said there's 60 folks on the companyright now. How many of them are in Thailandright now from your team?
So our team in total is 120 people.
Oh, 120. Okay, cool.
Yeah. And in Thailand, we have five people this year.

Okay, awesome. No, I think that's super cool. I know some teams have gotten together here and stuff, and it's really a fun place to kind of reconnect with your team, I found. Well, cool. Well, I just wanted to ask kind of as a closing, where can people find you on socials? Where's the best way to connect or to learn more?

Um, yeah, for sure. We covering almost all possible social media. So please, it's EverStake pool in Twitter, EverStake One websites, and all the LinkedTree, like LinkedIn, etc., etc., podcasts and all the other media. So we also have our own Discord for user support. So if you have any questions, EverStake website, Discord, please reach out to. We'll be happy to connect.

Thank you. Thank you so much for the amazing interview. Really appreciate the time and the information. Honestly, I really love that someone from also that you can research came on, because 99% of people cannot get into the level of detail that you did, and you explained it extremely well. So I really thank you for that, because for our audience, that is gold,right? Like, that is, that is literally why we do this, is to break down these concepts and to give people the understanding. So, you know, people really appreciate that. So thank you. And I hope you all enjoyed watching. So see you guys soon.
Thank you so much.
Thank you.
